questions.question: How many orders are in the dataset?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS order_count
FROM orders
questions.note: This counts every order regardless of status, since order-count questions include all statuses unless a filter is specified.

questions.question: How many sellers are on the platform?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS seller_count
FROM sellers
questions.note: This counts every row in `sellers`, including any seller with no order items, since the question asks about sellers on the platform rather than active sellers.

questions.question: What is the average review score across all reviews?
questions.sql:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(r.review_score)::numeric, 2) AS avg_review_score
FROM (
    SELECT DISTINCT review_id, review_score
    FROM order_reviews
) AS r
questions.note: I counted each review_id once, since one review can cover several orders, and included all order statuses because review questions are not filtered by status.

questions.question: What is the total value of all payments in the dataset?
questions.sql:
SELECT ROUND(SUM(payment_value), 2) AS total_payment_value
FROM order_payments
questions.note: This sums every payment row, including all order statuses, since the question asks about payments rather than revenue or sales.

questions.question: What is the average price of an order item?
questions.sql:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(price), 2) AS avg_item_price_brl
FROM order_items
questions.note: This averages `price` across all order item rows, excluding freight and including every order status, since the question doesn't mention revenue, sales, or items sold.

questions.question: How many products are there in each product category (English names)?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    COALESCE(product_category_name_english, 'unknown') AS category,
    COUNT(*) AS product_count
FROM products
GROUP BY COALESCE(product_category_name_english, 'unknown')
ORDER BY product_count DESC, category
questions.note: This counts every product in the catalog regardless of whether it has ever been sold. Products with no English category name are grouped as "unknown".

questions.question: How many distinct orders used each payment type?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    payment_type,
    COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS order_count
FROM order_payments
GROUP BY payment_type
ORDER BY order_count DESC
questions.note: An order paid with more than one method is counted once under each type it used, so the per-type counts can sum to more than the total number of distinct orders. No order-status filter is applied because the question doesn't mention revenue, sales, or purchases.

questions.question: What percentage of all orders have the status delivered?
questions.sql:
SELECT ROUND(
         100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE order_status = 'delivered') / COUNT(*),
         2
       ) AS delivered_pct
FROM orders
questions.note: This counts every order regardless of status, as the business rules specify for order counts, and divides the delivered count by the total.

questions.question: What is the average number of installments for credit card payments?
questions.sql:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(payment_installments)::numeric, 2) AS avg_installments
FROM order_payments
WHERE payment_type = 'credit_card'
  AND payment_installments > 0
questions.note: I averaged over credit-card payment rows and excluded the 0-installment rows, which the data notes flag as a data quality issue.

questions.question: What is the average order value, measured as total payment per order, for orders that were not canceled or unavailable?
questions.sql:
SELECT ROUND(SUM(p.payment_value) / COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id), 2) AS avg_order_value_brl
FROM orders o
JOIN order_payments p
  ON p.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
questions.note: I took "total payment per order" as the sum of `payment_value` across all payment rows, divided by the number of distinct non-canceled, non-unavailable orders that have a payment. The one order with no payment row is therefore left out of the denominator.

questions.question: What is the median total payment per order, across all orders?
questions.sql:
WITH order_totals AS (
    SELECT order_id, SUM(payment_value) AS total_payment
    FROM order_payments
    GROUP BY order_id
)
SELECT ROUND(
           CAST(percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY total_payment) AS numeric),
           2
       ) AS median_payment_per_order
FROM order_totals
questions.note: This includes all order statuses, since the question asks about payments rather than revenue or sales. The one order with no payment row is excluded because it has nothing to take a median of.

questions.question: How many unique customers live in the state of Rio de Janeiro (RJ)?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_unique_id) AS unique_customers_rj
FROM customers c
WHERE c.customer_state = 'RJ'
questions.note: This counts distinct people (`customer_unique_id`) by their customer state, including customers across all order statuses, since the question asks about customers rather than sales.

questions.question: How many products weigh more than 10 kg?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS products_over_10kg
FROM products
WHERE product_weight_g > 10000
questions.note: This counts every product in the catalog with a recorded weight above 10,000 g (10 kg). Products with a NULL weight are excluded automatically.

questions.question: How many order items cost more than 1,000 BRL?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS items_over_1000_brl
FROM order_items
WHERE price > 1000
questions.note: I counted every order item with a unit price above 1,000 BRL, excluding freight and without filtering by order status, since the question doesn't mention sales or revenue.

questions.question: How many delivered orders arrived after their estimated delivery date?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS late_delivered_orders
FROM orders
WHERE order_status = 'delivered'
  AND order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
  AND order_delivered_customer_date > order_estimated_delivery_date
questions.note: I counted only orders with status 'delivered' and a non-null customer delivery date, and treated "late" as a delivery date strictly after the estimated date. This should return 7,827, matching the dataset's stated late-delivery count.

questions.question: How many sellers are based in the state of São Paulo?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS sp_seller_count
FROM sellers
WHERE seller_state = 'SP'
questions.note: This counts every seller row whose `seller_state` is 'SP', using the seller's state rather than the messy `seller_city` field.

questions.question: How many 1-star reviews include a comment message?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT review_id) AS one_star_reviews_with_message
FROM order_reviews
WHERE review_score = 1
  AND review_comment_message IS NOT NULL
questions.note: I counted each review_id once, treated a comment as present when review_comment_message is not NULL, and included all order statuses since this is a review question.

questions.question: How many distinct orders were paid at least partly with a voucher?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS voucher_order_count
FROM order_payments
WHERE payment_type = 'voucher'
questions.note: This counts every order with at least one voucher payment row, across all order statuses, since this is a count question and not a revenue or sales question.

questions.question: How many products have no category?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS products_without_category
FROM products
WHERE product_category_name_english IS NULL
questions.note: I counted products where the English category name is NULL, since the category is unknown in that case. `product_id` is the primary key, so `COUNT(*)` counts distinct products.

questions.question: How many orders contain items from more than one seller?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS multi_seller_orders
FROM (
    SELECT order_id
    FROM order_items
    GROUP BY order_id
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT seller_id) > 1
) AS multi_seller
questions.note: This counts every order status, since the question doesn't mention revenue, sales, or items sold/bought, and it uses distinct `seller_id` values per order.

questions.question: List the cities in the state of Acre (AC) with the number of unique customers in each.
questions.sql:
SELECT
    c.customer_city AS city,
    COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_unique_id) AS unique_customers
FROM customers c
WHERE c.customer_state = 'AC'
GROUP BY c.customer_city
ORDER BY unique_customers DESC, city
questions.note: I counted unique people with `customer_unique_id` and included all order statuses, since this is a customer count rather than a revenue or sales question.

questions.question: How many orders were approved more than 24 hours after they were placed?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS orders_approved_over_24h_after_purchase
FROM orders
WHERE order_approved_at IS NOT NULL
  AND order_approved_at - order_purchase_timestamp > INTERVAL '24 hours'
questions.note: I counted every order status, since this is an order-count question, and excluded the 160 orders with no approval timestamp because their approval delay cannot be measured.

questions.question: Which 5 sellers generated the most revenue?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    oi.seller_id,
    s.seller_state,
    ROUND(SUM(oi.price), 2) AS revenue,
    COUNT(*) AS units_sold
FROM order_items AS oi
JOIN orders AS o
    ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
JOIN sellers AS s
    ON s.seller_id = oi.seller_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
GROUP BY oi.seller_id, s.seller_state
ORDER BY revenue DESC
LIMIT 5
questions.note: Revenue is item sales (sum of `price`, excluding freight) from orders that are not canceled or unavailable, since the question is seller-level and payments can't be split by seller.

questions.question: What is the total revenue by customer state?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    c.customer_state AS state,
    ROUND(SUM(p.payment_value), 2) AS total_revenue
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c
    ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
JOIN order_payments p
    ON p.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
GROUP BY c.customer_state
ORDER BY total_revenue DESC
questions.note: I used payment value as revenue, since this breakdown is by customer state rather than by product, category, or seller, and excluded canceled and unavailable orders.

questions.question: Which customer state has the highest average freight value per order item?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    c.customer_state AS state,
    ROUND(AVG(oi.freight_value), 2) AS avg_freight_per_item,
    COUNT(*) AS items
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
GROUP BY c.customer_state
ORDER BY avg_freight_per_item DESC
LIMIT 1
questions.note: I averaged `freight_value` over every order item, across all order statuses, since the question doesn't mention revenue, sales, or items sold, and I grouped by the customer's state.

questions.question: How many orders came from each customer state?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    c.customer_state AS customer_state,
    COUNT(*) AS order_count
FROM orders AS o
JOIN customers AS c
    ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
GROUP BY c.customer_state
ORDER BY order_count DESC
questions.note: This counts all orders regardless of status, since order counts are not filtered by status, and groups them by the customer's state from the customers table.

questions.question: Which 10 cities have the most unique customers?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    c.customer_city AS city,
    c.customer_state AS state,
    COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_unique_id) AS unique_customers
FROM customers c
GROUP BY c.customer_city, c.customer_state
ORDER BY unique_customers DESC, city, state
LIMIT 10
questions.note: I counted people with `customer_unique_id` and grouped by city and state together, since some city names may appear in more than one state. All order statuses are included, because this is a customer count rather than a revenue or sales measure.

questions.question: What is the average review score of orders paid with each payment type?
questions.sql:
WITH order_types AS (
    -- One row per order and payment method, so an order paid with two methods counts under both
    SELECT DISTINCT order_id, payment_type
    FROM order_payments
)
SELECT
    ot.payment_type,
    COUNT(*) AS review_count,
    ROUND(AVG(r.review_score), 2) AS avg_review_score
FROM order_types ot
JOIN order_reviews r
    ON r.order_id = ot.order_id
GROUP BY ot.payment_type
ORDER BY ot.payment_type
questions.note: I counted review rows per order, so a review covering several orders counts once for each order, and an order paid with two methods counts under both. Orders with no review are excluded, and all order statuses are included.

questions.question: What was the total freight charged on items in the furniture_decor category?
questions.sql:
SELECT ROUND(SUM(oi.freight_value), 2) AS total_freight_brl
FROM order_items oi
JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
WHERE p.product_category_name_english = 'furniture_decor'
questions.note: I included all order statuses because the question asks about freight charged on items, not revenue, sales, or items sold, so the canceled/unavailable exclusion doesn't apply.

questions.question: What was the total revenue from customers in Minas Gerais (MG)?
questions.sql:
SELECT ROUND(SUM(p.payment_value), 2) AS total_revenue_mg_brl
FROM order_payments p
JOIN orders o
  ON o.order_id = p.order_id
JOIN customers c
  ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
WHERE c.customer_state = 'MG'
  AND o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
questions.note: I used payment value as revenue (the default for order-level totals), grouped by the customer's state, and excluded canceled and unavailable orders.

questions.question: What is the English name of the product category 'cama_mesa_banho'?
questions.sql:
SELECT product_category_name_english AS english_name
FROM category_translation
WHERE product_category_name = 'cama_mesa_banho'
questions.note: I looked up the name in `category_translation`, which maps each Portuguese category to its English name.

questions.question: Which product category has the highest average review score among categories with at least 100 reviewed orders?
questions.sql:
WITH order_cats AS (
    -- one row per (order, category) so multi-unit or multi-category orders aren't double counted
    SELECT DISTINCT oi.order_id,
           COALESCE(p.product_category_name_english, 'unknown') AS category
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
),
cat_reviews AS (
    SELECT oc.category, oc.order_id, r.review_score
    FROM order_cats oc
    JOIN order_reviews r ON r.order_id = oc.order_id
)
SELECT category,
       COUNT(DISTINCT order_id)          AS reviewed_orders,
       ROUND(AVG(review_score), 2)       AS avg_review_score
FROM cat_reviews
GROUP BY category
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) >= 100
ORDER BY AVG(review_score) DESC, category
LIMIT 1
questions.note: I counted reviewed orders as orders with at least one review, averaged over the review rows of those orders (per the review conventions), and kept orders of every status. The 'unknown' bucket for products without a category is included as a candidate, so it would be returned if it had the top score.

questions.question: Which 3 sellers have the highest average review score among sellers with at least 50 reviewed orders?
questions.sql:
WITH seller_orders AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT seller_id, order_id
    FROM order_items
),
seller_reviews AS (
    SELECT so.seller_id, so.order_id, r.review_score
    FROM seller_orders so
    JOIN order_reviews r ON r.order_id = so.order_id
)
SELECT
    sr.seller_id,
    s.seller_state AS seller_state,
    COUNT(DISTINCT sr.order_id) AS reviewed_orders,
    ROUND(AVG(sr.review_score)::numeric, 2) AS avg_review_score
FROM seller_reviews sr
JOIN sellers s ON s.seller_id = sr.seller_id
GROUP BY sr.seller_id, s.seller_state
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT sr.order_id) >= 50
ORDER BY avg_review_score DESC, reviewed_orders DESC
LIMIT 3
questions.note: I counted a seller's reviewed orders as distinct orders containing that seller's items that have at least one review, and averaged scores over the review rows for those orders, per the review conventions. Orders of all statuses are included, since the question doesn't ask about sales or revenue.

questions.question: How many unique customers bought from a seller located in a different state from their own?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_unique_id) AS unique_customers
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c
  ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
JOIN order_items oi
  ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
JOIN sellers s
  ON s.seller_id = oi.seller_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
  AND c.customer_state <> s.seller_state
questions.note: I treated "bought" as a sales question, so canceled and unavailable orders are excluded, and I counted distinct people via customer_unique_id rather than per-order customer_id.

questions.question: What is the average price of items sold by sellers in each seller state?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    s.seller_state,
    ROUND(AVG(oi.price), 2) AS avg_item_price,
    COUNT(*) AS items_sold
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o
    ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
JOIN sellers s
    ON s.seller_id = oi.seller_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
GROUP BY s.seller_state
ORDER BY s.seller_state
questions.note: I excluded canceled and unavailable orders because the question asks about items sold, and I averaged over item rows (excluding freight) by seller state.

questions.question: How many orders were placed in each year?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM order_purchase_timestamp)::INT AS order_year,
    COUNT(*) AS order_count
FROM orders
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1
questions.note: This counts all order statuses, as order counts do. The 2016 row is sparse (only about 329 orders), and 2018 covers only January to October, with September and October nearly empty, so both years are incomplete.

questions.question: Which month had the most orders?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    date_trunc('month', order_purchase_timestamp)::date AS month,
    COUNT(*) AS order_count
FROM orders
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY order_count DESC
LIMIT 1
questions.note: This counts all order statuses, as the rules specify for order counts, and groups by the purchase month. The sparse 2016 months and the incomplete 2018-09/10 months can't be the peak, so they don't affect the result.

questions.question: What was the average review score for each month of 2018, based on when the review was created?
questions.sql:
WITH unique_reviews AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT review_id, review_score, review_creation_date
    FROM order_reviews
    WHERE review_creation_date >= '2018-01-01'
      AND review_creation_date <  '2019-01-01'
)
SELECT
    DATE_TRUNC('month', review_creation_date)::date AS month,
    COUNT(*)                                        AS review_count,
    ROUND(AVG(review_score), 2)                     AS avg_score
FROM unique_reviews
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1
questions.note: I counted each review_id once, using its creation date, and kept all order statuses since this is a review question. The feed effectively ends in 2018-08, so the September and October 2018 rows rest on very few orders and should be read with caution.

questions.question: What was the total revenue in Q4 2017?
questions.sql:
SELECT ROUND(SUM(p.payment_value), 2) AS total_revenue_brl
FROM orders o
JOIN order_payments p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp >= TIMESTAMP '2017-10-01'
  AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  TIMESTAMP '2018-01-01'
  AND o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
questions.note: I used payment value as the revenue measure (what customers paid, including freight and installment interest) and excluded canceled and unavailable orders, filtering by purchase timestamp for Oct to Dec 2017.

questions.question: On which day of the week (e.g. Monday) are the most orders placed?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    TRIM(TO_CHAR(order_purchase_timestamp, 'Day')) AS day_of_week,
    COUNT(*) AS order_count
FROM orders
GROUP BY TRIM(TO_CHAR(order_purchase_timestamp, 'Day'))
ORDER BY order_count DESC
LIMIT 1
questions.note: Assumption: order counts include all statuses, and the day is based on `order_purchase_timestamp` (local time).

questions.question: For each purchase month of 2017, what was the average delivery time in days (as a decimal) for delivered orders?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    to_char(date_trunc('month', order_purchase_timestamp), 'YYYY-MM') AS purchase_month,
    ROUND(AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (order_delivered_customer_date - order_purchase_timestamp)) / 86400.0), 2) AS avg_delivery_days
FROM orders
WHERE order_status = 'delivered'
  AND order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
  AND order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-01-01'
  AND order_purchase_timestamp <  '2018-01-01'
GROUP BY date_trunc('month', order_purchase_timestamp)
ORDER BY date_trunc('month', order_purchase_timestamp)
questions.note: I measured delivery time from purchase to customer delivery as fractional days, using only delivered orders with a delivery date, grouped by purchase month.

questions.question: How many orders were placed on Black Friday 2017 (November 24, 2017)?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS black_friday_orders
FROM orders
WHERE order_purchase_timestamp >= TIMESTAMP '2017-11-24 00:00:00'
  AND order_purchase_timestamp <  TIMESTAMP '2017-11-25 00:00:00'
questions.note: This counts all orders regardless of status, since the question asks about orders placed rather than sales or revenue, and uses the purchase timestamp in local time.

questions.question: Which product category had the largest increase in units sold from January–August 2017 to January–August 2018?
questions.sql:
WITH units AS (
    SELECT COALESCE(p.product_category_name_english, 'unknown') AS category,
           EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.order_purchase_timestamp)::int AS yr,
           COUNT(*) AS units
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    LEFT JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
      AND EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.order_purchase_timestamp) BETWEEN 1 AND 8
      AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.order_purchase_timestamp) IN (2017, 2018)
    GROUP BY 1, 2
)
SELECT category,
       COALESCE(SUM(units) FILTER (WHERE yr = 2017), 0) AS units_2017,
       COALESCE(SUM(units) FILTER (WHERE yr = 2018), 0) AS units_2018,
       COALESCE(SUM(units) FILTER (WHERE yr = 2018), 0)
         - COALESCE(SUM(units) FILTER (WHERE yr = 2017), 0) AS unit_increase
FROM units
GROUP BY category
ORDER BY unit_increase DESC
LIMIT 1
questions.note: I measured "increase" as the absolute change in units (2018 minus 2017, Jan–Aug, excluding canceled and unavailable orders), and kept products with no category as "unknown" rather than dropping them.

questions.question: Which month of 2018 had the most orders?
questions.sql:
SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', o.order_purchase_timestamp)::date AS order_month,
       COUNT(*) AS order_count
FROM orders o
WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-01-01'
  AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  '2019-01-01'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY order_count DESC
LIMIT 1
questions.note: This counts all order statuses, as the rules specify for order counts. The result is the single top month, and 2018 months are complete through August. September and October 2018 are partial feed months, but they cannot be the top month here.

questions.question: Which 5 product categories had the largest drop in revenue from July 2018 to August 2018?
questions.sql:
WITH item_rev AS (
    SELECT
        COALESCE(p.product_category_name_english, 'unknown') AS category,
        SUM(CASE WHEN o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-07-01'
                  AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  '2018-08-01'
                 THEN oi.price ELSE 0 END) AS jul_revenue,
        SUM(CASE WHEN o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-08-01'
                  AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  '2018-09-01'
                 THEN oi.price ELSE 0 END) AS aug_revenue
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN orders o
      ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    LEFT JOIN products p
      ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-07-01'
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  '2018-09-01'
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT
    category,
    ROUND(jul_revenue, 2)               AS july_2018_revenue,
    ROUND(aug_revenue, 2)               AS august_2018_revenue,
    ROUND(jul_revenue - aug_revenue, 2) AS revenue_drop
FROM item_rev
ORDER BY revenue_drop DESC
LIMIT 5
questions.note: I measured revenue as item price (excluding freight) from order_items, excluded canceled and unavailable orders, and grouped by purchase month. Drop is July minus August, so a positive value means revenue fell. Products without a category are reported as "unknown". July and August 2018 are the two complete months of Q3 2018.

questions.question: What was the month-over-month percentage change in the number of orders for each month from January to August 2018?
questions.sql:
WITH monthly AS (
    SELECT date_trunc('month', order_purchase_timestamp)::date AS month_start,
           COUNT(*) AS orders
    FROM orders
    GROUP BY 1
),
with_prev AS (
    SELECT month_start,
           orders,
           LAG(orders) OVER (ORDER BY month_start) AS prev_orders
    FROM monthly
)
SELECT to_char(month_start, 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
       orders AS order_count,
       prev_orders AS prev_month_orders,
       ROUND(100.0 * (orders - prev_orders) / NULLIF(prev_orders, 0), 2) AS mom_pct_change
FROM with_prev
WHERE month_start >= DATE '2018-01-01'
  AND month_start <  DATE '2018-09-01'
ORDER BY month_start
questions.note: The query counts all order statuses, since the question asks about order counts rather than revenue or sales. January's change is measured against December 2017, which is computed from the full monthly series before filtering to Jan–Aug 2018.

questions.question: For each customer state, which product category generated the most revenue?
questions.sql:
WITH cat_rev AS (
    SELECT
        c.customer_state AS state,
        COALESCE(p.product_category_name_english, 'unknown') AS category,
        SUM(oi.price) AS revenue,
        COUNT(*) AS units
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
    GROUP BY 1, 2
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT
        state,
        category,
        revenue,
        units,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY state ORDER BY revenue DESC, category) AS rn
    FROM cat_rev
)
SELECT
    state AS customer_state,
    category AS top_category,
    ROUND(revenue, 2) AS revenue,
    units AS units_sold
FROM ranked
WHERE rn = 1
ORDER BY state
questions.note: Revenue here is item sales (SUM of `price`, excluding freight), since the question breaks revenue down by category, and canceled and unavailable orders are excluded. Products with no category are reported as "unknown".

questions.question: What was the 3-month moving average of monthly revenue (the current month and the two before it) for each month from January to August 2018?
questions.sql:
WITH monthly AS (
    SELECT date_trunc('month', o.order_purchase_timestamp) AS month_start,
           SUM(p.payment_value) AS revenue
    FROM orders o
    JOIN order_payments p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
    GROUP BY 1
),
smoothed AS (
    SELECT month_start,
           revenue,
           AVG(revenue) OVER (
               ORDER BY month_start
               ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
           ) AS moving_avg_3m
    FROM monthly
)
SELECT to_char(month_start, 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
       ROUND(revenue, 2) AS revenue,
       ROUND(moving_avg_3m, 2) AS moving_avg_3m
FROM smoothed
WHERE month_start >= DATE '2018-01-01'
  AND month_start <  DATE '2018-09-01'
ORDER BY month_start
questions.note: I used payment revenue (SUM of `payment_value`) with canceled and unavailable orders excluded, and computed the window over all months so January 2018 averages in November and December 2017.

questions.question: Which 5 sellers had the highest item revenue in 2018, and what percentage of total 2018 item revenue did each account for?
questions.sql:
WITH item_2018 AS (
    SELECT oi.seller_id, oi.price
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp >= TIMESTAMP '2018-01-01'
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  TIMESTAMP '2019-01-01'
      AND o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
),
seller_rev AS (
    SELECT seller_id, SUM(price) AS item_revenue
    FROM item_2018
    GROUP BY seller_id
)
SELECT s.seller_id,
       s.seller_state,
       ROUND(sr.item_revenue, 2) AS item_revenue,
       ROUND(100.0 * sr.item_revenue / SUM(sr.item_revenue) OVER (), 2) AS pct_of_2018_item_revenue
FROM seller_rev sr
JOIN sellers s ON s.seller_id = sr.seller_id
ORDER BY sr.item_revenue DESC
LIMIT 5
questions.note: Assumes "item revenue" means SUM(order_items.price) excluding freight, with canceled and unavailable orders excluded and 2018 defined by order_purchase_timestamp; the percentage denominator is total item revenue across all sellers for the same filters.

questions.question: For 2017 and 2018 separately, what were the top 3 product categories by units sold?
questions.sql:
WITH sold AS (
    SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.order_purchase_timestamp)::int AS yr,
           COALESCE(p.product_category_name_english, 'unknown') AS category,
           COUNT(*) AS units
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    LEFT JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-01-01'
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2019-01-01'
    GROUP BY 1, 2
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT yr, category, units,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY yr ORDER BY units DESC, category) AS rnk
    FROM sold
)
SELECT yr AS year,
       rnk AS rank,
       category,
       units AS units_sold
FROM ranked
WHERE rnk <= 3
ORDER BY yr, rnk
questions.note: I counted units as order_items rows, excluded canceled and unavailable orders because the question asks about units sold, and grouped products with no category under "unknown" instead of dropping them. Ties within a year are broken alphabetically by category name.

questions.question: What percentage of all orders came from each customer state?

    ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id)
          / SUM(COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id)) OVER (), 2) AS pct_of_orders
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c
  ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
GROUP BY c.customer_state
ORDER BY pct_of_orders DESC

questions.question: Which month in 2017 had the largest increase in orders compared with the previous month?
questions.sql:
WITH monthly AS (
    SELECT date_trunc('month', order_purchase_timestamp)::date AS month_start,
           COUNT(*) AS orders
    FROM orders
    WHERE order_purchase_timestamp >= '2016-12-01'
      AND order_purchase_timestamp <  '2018-01-01'
    GROUP BY 1
),
mom AS (
    SELECT month_start,
           orders,
           LAG(orders) OVER (ORDER BY month_start) AS prev_orders
    FROM monthly
)
SELECT to_char(month_start, 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
       orders,
       prev_orders AS previous_month_orders,
       orders - prev_orders AS order_increase,
       ROUND(100.0 * (orders - prev_orders) / NULLIF(prev_orders, 0), 2) AS pct_increase
FROM mom
WHERE month_start >= '2017-02-01'  -- Jan 2017 is excluded: its prior month (Dec 2016) is a sparse, incomplete period
ORDER BY order_increase DESC
LIMIT 1
questions.note: I counted all order statuses, since the question asks about orders rather than revenue or sales, and I left out January 2017 because its comparison base, December 2016, has only one order.

questions.question: For each seller state, which seller has the highest revenue?
questions.sql:
WITH seller_revenue AS (
    SELECT
        s.seller_state,
        oi.seller_id,
        SUM(oi.price) AS revenue
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    JOIN sellers s ON s.seller_id = oi.seller_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
    GROUP BY s.seller_state, oi.seller_id
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT
        seller_state,
        seller_id,
        revenue,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY seller_state
            ORDER BY revenue DESC, seller_id
        ) AS rn
    FROM seller_revenue
)
SELECT
    seller_state AS state,
    seller_id,
    ROUND(revenue, 2) AS revenue_brl
FROM ranked
WHERE rn = 1
ORDER BY state
questions.note: I measured revenue as item sales (SUM of `price`, excluding freight) since this is a breakdown by seller, and excluded canceled and unavailable orders. Ties within a state are broken by seller_id.

questions.question: How are we doing?
questions.sql:
WITH period AS (
    SELECT *
    FROM orders
    WHERE order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-01-01'
      AND order_purchase_timestamp <  '2018-09-01'
),
order_paid AS (
    SELECT order_id, SUM(payment_value) AS paid
    FROM order_payments
    GROUP BY order_id
),
monthly_sales AS (
    SELECT
        date_trunc('month', p.order_purchase_timestamp) AS month_start,
        COUNT(*) AS orders_placed,
        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE p.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')) AS sales_orders,
        SUM(op.paid) FILTER (WHERE p.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')) AS revenue,
        SUM(op.paid) FILTER (WHERE p.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable'))
            / NULLIF(COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE p.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')), 0) AS avg_order_value
    FROM period p
    LEFT JOIN order_paid op ON op.order_id = p.order_id
    GROUP BY 1
),
monthly_reviews AS (
    SELECT
        date_trunc('month', p.order_purchase_timestamp) AS month_start,
        AVG(r.review_score) AS avg_review_score
    FROM period p
    JOIN order_reviews r ON r.order_id = p.order_id
    GROUP BY 1
),
monthly_delivery AS (
    SELECT
        date_trunc('month', p.order_purchase_timestamp) AS month_start,
        COUNT(*) AS delivered_orders,
        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE p.order_delivered_customer_date > p.order_estimated_delivery_date) AS late_orders
    FROM period p
    WHERE p.order_status = 'delivered'
      AND p.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT
    to_char(s.month_start, 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
    s.sales_orders AS sales_orders,
    ROUND(s.revenue, 2) AS revenue_brl,
    ROUND(s.avg_order_value, 2) AS avg_order_value_brl,
    ROUND(r.avg_review_score, 2) AS avg_review_score,
    ROUND(100.0 * d.late_orders / NULLIF(d.delivered_orders, 0), 2) AS late_delivery_pct
FROM monthly_sales s
LEFT JOIN monthly_reviews r ON r.month_start = s.month_start
LEFT JOIN monthly_delivery d ON d.month_start = s.month_start
ORDER BY s.month_start
questions.note: This shows a monthly health check from 2017-01 to 2018-08, the period with reliable data; sales exclude canceled and unavailable orders, and revenue is payments collected.

questions.question: Who are our best customers?

valid_orders AS (

questions.question: What was the recent trend?

questions.question: What percentage of unique customers have placed more than one order?

questions.question: How many orders have a total payment that differs from the sum of their items' price plus freight by more than 1 BRL?
questions.sql:
WITH pay AS (
    SELECT order_id, SUM(payment_value) AS paid_total
    FROM order_payments
    GROUP BY order_id
),
itm AS (
    SELECT order_id, SUM(price + freight_value) AS item_total
    FROM order_items
    GROUP BY order_id
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS mismatched_orders
FROM pay p
JOIN itm i USING (order_id)
WHERE ABS(p.paid_total - i.item_total) > 1

questions.question: How many sellers made at least one sale in every month from January to June 2018?

WITH seller_months AS (

    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id

questions.question: What was the total revenue from orders that include at least one bed_bath_table item?

    JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id

questions.question: What were the total revenue and the total freight for each customer state?
questions.sql:
WITH pay AS (
    SELECT order_id, SUM(payment_value) AS paid
    FROM order_payments
    GROUP BY order_id
),
frt AS (
    SELECT order_id, SUM(freight_value) AS freight
    FROM order_items
    GROUP BY order_id
)
SELECT
    c.customer_state AS customer_state,
    ROUND(SUM(p.paid), 2) AS total_revenue,
    ROUND(SUM(f.freight), 2) AS total_freight
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
LEFT JOIN pay p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
LEFT JOIN frt f ON f.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
GROUP BY c.customer_state
ORDER BY c.customer_state
questions.note: I used payments as the revenue measure, since the breakdown is by customer state rather than by product, category or seller, and freight comes from order_items. Each order's payments and freight are aggregated separately before joining, so neither sum is inflated.

questions.question: For each customer state with at least 1,000 orders, what is the average order value (total payment per order)?
questions.sql:
WITH order_totals AS (
    SELECT order_id, SUM(payment_value) AS total_payment
    FROM order_payments
    GROUP BY order_id
)
SELECT
    c.customer_state AS state,
    COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS orders,
    ROUND(AVG(t.total_payment), 2) AS avg_order_value
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
JOIN order_totals t ON t.order_id = o.order_id
GROUP BY c.customer_state
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) >= 1000
ORDER BY avg_order_value DESC
questions.note: I took "total payment per order" to mean summed order_payments.payment_value per order, kept all order statuses since the question doesn't mention revenue or sales, and counted only orders that have at least one payment.

questions.question: By what percentage did revenue in January–August 2018 grow compared with January–August 2017?
questions.sql:
WITH period_revenue AS (
    SELECT
        EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.order_purchase_timestamp)::int AS yr,
        SUM(p.payment_value) AS revenue
    FROM orders o
    JOIN order_payments p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
      AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.order_purchase_timestamp) IN (2017, 2018)
      AND EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.order_purchase_timestamp) BETWEEN 1 AND 8
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT
    ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN yr = 2017 THEN revenue END), 2) AS revenue_jan_aug_2017,
    ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN yr = 2018 THEN revenue END), 2) AS revenue_jan_aug_2018,
    ROUND(
        100.0 * (MAX(CASE WHEN yr = 2018 THEN revenue END) - MAX(CASE WHEN yr = 2017 THEN revenue END))
        / MAX(CASE WHEN yr = 2017 THEN revenue END),
        2
    ) AS growth_pct
FROM period_revenue
questions.note: I used payment totals (SUM of `payment_value`) as revenue, excluding canceled and unavailable orders, and matched periods on `order_purchase_timestamp` for January to August in each year.

questions.question: What was the cancellation rate (percentage of orders canceled) for each month of 2017?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    DATE_TRUNC('month', order_purchase_timestamp)::date AS month,
    COUNT(*) AS total_orders,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE order_status = 'canceled') AS canceled_orders,
    ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE order_status = 'canceled') / COUNT(*), 2) AS cancellation_rate_pct
FROM orders
WHERE order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-01-01'
  AND order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-01-01'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1
questions.note: I counted all orders in each month as the denominator and only `canceled` status as cancellations, so `unavailable` orders are not counted as canceled.

questions.question: For the top 5 product categories by 2017 revenue, what was each category's revenue in January–August 2018?
questions.sql:
WITH item_rev AS (
    SELECT COALESCE(p.product_category_name_english, 'unknown') AS category,
           o.order_purchase_timestamp AS ts,
           oi.price
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    LEFT JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
),
top5 AS (
    SELECT category, SUM(price) AS rev_2017
    FROM item_rev
    WHERE ts >= '2017-01-01' AND ts < '2018-01-01'
    GROUP BY category
    ORDER BY rev_2017 DESC
    LIMIT 5
)
SELECT t.category,
       ROUND(t.rev_2017, 2) AS revenue_2017,
       ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(i.price) FILTER (
             WHERE i.ts >= '2018-01-01' AND i.ts < '2018-09-01'), 0), 2) AS revenue_2018_jan_aug
FROM top5 t
LEFT JOIN item_rev i ON i.category = t.category
GROUP BY t.category, t.rev_2017
ORDER BY t.rev_2017 DESC
questions.note: I used item sales (SUM of `order_items.price`, excluding freight) since this is a category breakdown, and excluded canceled and unavailable orders. Products with no category are grouped as "unknown" and can appear in the top 5 if they rank there.

questions.question: What percentage of item revenue in January–August 2018 came from the 10 products with the highest revenue in that period?
questions.sql:
WITH item_sales AS (
    SELECT oi.product_id, oi.price
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-01-01'
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  '2018-09-01'
),
product_rev AS (
    SELECT product_id, SUM(price) AS revenue
    FROM item_sales
    GROUP BY product_id
),
top10 AS (
    SELECT product_id, revenue
    FROM product_rev
    ORDER BY revenue DESC
    LIMIT 10
)
SELECT
    ROUND((SELECT SUM(revenue) FROM top10), 2) AS top10_revenue,
    ROUND((SELECT SUM(revenue) FROM product_rev), 2) AS total_item_revenue,
    ROUND(100.0 * (SELECT SUM(revenue) FROM top10)
          / NULLIF((SELECT SUM(revenue) FROM product_rev), 0), 2) AS top10_share_pct
questions.note: I measured item revenue as SUM(order_items.price) (excluding freight) for orders placed Jan 1 to Aug 31, 2018, excluding canceled and unavailable orders.

questions.question: Which product category has the highest percentage of late deliveries, among categories with at least 500 delivered orders?
questions.sql:
WITH delivered AS (
    SELECT o.order_id,
           (o.order_delivered_customer_date > o.order_estimated_delivery_date) AS is_late
    FROM orders o
    WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
      AND o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
),
order_categories AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT oi.order_id,
           COALESCE(p.product_category_name_english, 'unknown') AS category
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
    JOIN delivered d ON d.order_id = oi.order_id
)
SELECT oc.category,
       COUNT(*) AS delivered_orders,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE d.is_late) AS late_orders,
       ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE d.is_late) / COUNT(*), 2) AS late_pct
FROM order_categories oc
JOIN delivered d ON d.order_id = oc.order_id
GROUP BY oc.category
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 500
ORDER BY late_pct DESC
LIMIT 1
questions.note: I counted each order once per category it contains, using delivered orders with a delivery date, and kept products with no category as "unknown" rather than dropping them.

questions.question: How much lower is the average review score for delivered orders that arrived late than for delivered orders that arrived on time?
questions.sql:
WITH delivered AS (
    SELECT
        order_id,
        (order_delivered_customer_date > order_estimated_delivery_date) AS is_late
    FROM orders
    WHERE order_status = 'delivered'
      AND order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
    ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN d.is_late THEN r.review_score END), 2)      AS late_avg_score,
    ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN NOT d.is_late THEN r.review_score END), 2)  AS on_time_avg_score,
    ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN NOT d.is_late THEN r.review_score END)
        - AVG(CASE WHEN d.is_late THEN r.review_score END), 2)      AS score_gap_on_time_minus_late
FROM delivered d
JOIN order_reviews r ON r.order_id = d.order_id
questions.note: I assumed "on time" means delivered on or before the estimated date, and averaged over review rows for those orders (per the per-order convention), so a review covering several orders counts once per order. A positive gap means late deliveries score lower.

questions.question: For each month from January to August 2018, what was the cumulative revenue since the start of 2018?
questions.sql:
WITH monthly AS (
    SELECT
        date_trunc('month', o.order_purchase_timestamp)::date AS month_start,
        SUM(p.payment_value) AS revenue
    FROM orders o
    JOIN order_payments p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-01-01'
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  '2018-09-01'
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT
    to_char(month_start, 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
    ROUND(revenue, 2) AS monthly_revenue,
    ROUND(SUM(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month_start), 2) AS cumulative_revenue
FROM monthly
ORDER BY month_start
questions.note: I used payment-based revenue (SUM of `payment_value`) because this is an order-level total, excluded canceled and unavailable orders, and bucketed by `order_purchase_timestamp`.

questions.question: Show me last year's numbers.
questions.sql:
WITH pay AS (
    SELECT order_id, SUM(payment_value) AS paid
    FROM order_payments
    GROUP BY order_id
),
items AS (
    SELECT order_id,
           SUM(price) AS item_price,
           SUM(freight_value) AS freight,
           COUNT(*) AS units
    FROM order_items
    GROUP BY order_id
),
orders_2017 AS (
    SELECT o.order_id, o.order_status, c.customer_unique_id
    FROM orders o
    JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-01-01'
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-01-01'
)
SELECT
    COUNT(*) AS orders_placed,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')) AS sales_orders,
    ROUND(SUM(p.paid) FILTER (WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')), 2) AS payment_revenue,
    ROUND(SUM(i.item_price) FILTER (WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')), 2) AS item_sales,
    ROUND(SUM(i.freight) FILTER (WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')), 2) AS freight_sales,
    SUM(i.units) FILTER (WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')) AS units_sold,
    ROUND(
        SUM(p.paid) FILTER (WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable'))
        / NULLIF(COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')), 0),
        2) AS avg_order_value,
    COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_unique_id) FILTER (WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')) AS unique_customers
FROM orders_2017 o
LEFT JOIN pay p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
LEFT JOIN items i ON i.order_id = o.order_id
questions.note: I took "last year" to mean calendar 2017, the most recent complete year, since 2018 is only partially covered. Revenue is payment-based, and canceled and unavailable orders are excluded from the sales figures.

questions.question: Which products perform best?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    oi.product_id,
    COALESCE(p.product_category_name_english, 'unknown') AS category,
    COUNT(*) AS units_sold,
    ROUND(SUM(oi.price), 2) AS item_revenue,
    ROUND(AVG(oi.price), 2) AS avg_unit_price
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o
    ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
LEFT JOIN products p
    ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
GROUP BY oi.product_id, COALESCE(p.product_category_name_english, 'unknown')
ORDER BY item_revenue DESC
LIMIT 10
questions.note: I interpreted "perform best" as highest item revenue (SUM of price, excluding freight) among non-canceled, non-unavailable orders, and show the top 10 products.

questions.question: What will our revenue be next month?
questions.sql:
WITH monthly AS (
    SELECT date_trunc('month', o.order_purchase_timestamp)::date AS month,
           SUM(p.payment_value) AS revenue
    FROM orders o
    JOIN order_payments p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-01-01'
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-09-01'
    GROUP BY 1
),
last3 AS (
    SELECT month, revenue
    FROM monthly
    ORDER BY month DESC
    LIMIT 3
)
SELECT (SELECT MAX(month) FROM monthly) + INTERVAL '1 month' AS forecast_month,
       ROUND((SELECT AVG(revenue) FROM last3), 2) AS forecast_revenue,
       ROUND((SELECT revenue FROM monthly ORDER BY month DESC LIMIT 1), 2) AS last_complete_month_revenue
questions.note: This is a naive baseline, not a statistical forecast: it averages payment revenue over the last three complete months (Jun to Aug 2018), excluding canceled and unavailable orders. The data feed effectively ends in August 2018 (September 2018 has only 16 orders), so the true next month is not covered by the data and the figure should be treated as a rough estimate.

questions.question: Which product has the most appealing name?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    p.product_id,
    COALESCE(p.product_category_name_english, 'unknown') AS category,
    p.product_name_length AS name_length
FROM products p
WHERE p.product_name_length IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY p.product_name_length DESC, p.product_id
LIMIT 1
questions.note: The dataset has no product names, so "appealing" cannot be measured. This query uses the longest name length as a weak proxy, and the result should not be read as a real measure of appeal.
